meta.title: Romanian Phrases and Expressions
meta.subtitle: 372 expressions · 95 everyday, 233 idioms, 44 proverbs · both directions
meta.desc: 372 Romanian set phrases, idioms and proverbs, in three subdecks: 95 everyday phrases, 233 idioms and 44 proverbs. Both study directions come as two cards of one expression — Romanian → English (see the Romanian, recall the meaning) and English → Romanian (see an English meaning, recall the Romanian) — each with a schedule of its own. This is a companion to the six level decks, Romanian A1 to C2, and not one of them: a level is a list of words, and an expression is a unit a list of words cannot see. Nothing here is taught by any of the six, so the two can be studied together without repeating an entry. The PHRASES are the expressions Wiktionary files as phrases or interjections and does not mark as idiomatic — mostly the everyday formulas a Romanian speaker uses as one piece (nu știu, să mergem, îmi pare rău …). The IDIOMS are expressions whose meaning is not their words' (din ce în ce, pierde trenul, face față …), most of them verbs, given like every verb on the shelf with the infinitive's a; and the PROVERBS the sayings Wiktionary files as proverbs (ochii care nu se văd se uită, prietenul la nevoie se cunoaște, cine râde la urmă râde mai bine …), each glossed with the English proverb that says the same where there is one. Within each subdeck the expressions come in the order of how many of Tatoeba's Romanian sentences contain them, an expression that is a verb being counted with its verb in any form; only 88 of the 372 are found there at all, and the rest follow in the order of how common their rarest word is in film and television subtitles. 54 of the 372 carry Wiktionary's pronunciation in the International Phonetic Alphabet. Real example sentences come with 87 of the 372 expressions, three apiece for 33, with the expression picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Expressions, meanings, pronunciation and the idiom and proverb labels: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Order: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR, then a word list built from OpenSubtitles (hermitdave/FrequencyWords, CC BY-SA 4.0). Example sentences: Tatoeba, CC BY 2.0 FR.
